253370.why: The kouros has stood with one foot forward and a small smile for 2,600 years. Young, upright, and about to walk.

254587.why: A marble harp player, head tipped back, lost in a tune from nearly five thousand years ago.

247967.why: A small bronze diskos thrower caught at the top of the wind-up. All of the energy is still to come.

252890.why: The grave stele of a little girl holding her two pet doves. Quiet, tender and very old.

248483.why: A family group on a grave marker, clasping hands. People holding on to each other, carved in marble.

248140.why: A marble lion that once guarded a tomb, mouth open, still keeping watch.

254502.why: Eros, the god of love, fast asleep on a rock with his wings folded. Permission to rest.

247017.why: A whole Roman bedroom from a villa buried by Vesuvius, painted red and gold. Step inside and close the door on the day.

250945.why: Perseus swooping in to rescue Andromeda, painted on a Roman wall in a landscape full of air and distance.

247993.why: Augustus, carved to look calm and ageless. A face made to say that everything is under control.

253592.why: Caracalla scowling over his shoulder. The most honest portrait of a bad mood in the building.

248132.why: A Roman marble of an old market woman on her way to a festival, basket in hand, tired and determined.

256403.why: The Three Graces with their arms around each other. Friendship, in marble, for two thousand years.

254819.why: A sarcophagus crowded with Dionysos, panthers, satyrs and the four seasons. A party carved in stone.

247117.why: An eight-foot bronze of the emperor Trebonianus Gallus, one of very few to survive. Heavy, odd and impossible to ignore.

250551.why: An amphora by Exekias, the finest of the black-figure painters. Small figures doing precise things, beautifully.
